title: Lumbar range of motion
summary: Apply pure moments, with a preload where listed, to intact lumbar specimens and report the rotation of each segment or the whole specimen.
simulate: Build the intact ligamentous specimen of the simulation (FSU at each listed level, or the multi-level L1-S1 / L1-L5 / L1-L4 specimen); fix the caudal vertebra (sacrum).
Apply a pure moment to the cranial vertebra in the simulation's direction and sweep it over the listed moments (or sweep the follower load at 8/6 Nm); other 5 DOF free.

Preload only if listed: follower load along a path through the vertebral centres, or a fixed vertical axial force. Panjabi 1994 tasks: 100 N compression kept along the specimen axis during bending (model it as a follower load or an axial load that rotates with the top vertebra).
One-direction simulations: neutral to peak. "L+R" and "Flexion+extension": sum of both directions (full range) at each moment.
Report every listed output (segmental ROM per level, total ROM, neutral zone) as one curve over the sweep, loading branch.

outputs.label: Segmental ROM
outputs.definition: ROM = rotation of the upper vertebra relative to the lower at peak moment, loading branch (deg)

outputs.label: Total ROM
outputs.definition: Total ROM = rotation of the top vertebra relative to the bottom one (sacrum) at peak moment, loading branch (deg)

outputs.label: Neutral zone
outputs.definition: Neutral zone = rotation between loading and unloading branches at 0 Nm (third cycle), both directions summed (deg)

notes: One direction (e.g. Flexion) and both directions summed (Flexion+extension, L+R) are separate tasks; never compare across them.
Segmental tasks mix isolated FSUs and segments inside multi-level specimens (see ref notes).
Many refs are medians (Wilke 2025, Heuer), not pooled; Wilke 2025, Kettler 2011 and Heuer share Ulm specimens.
agent_prompt: You have a finite element model of the intact ligamentous human lumbar spine (no muscles). Run the 16 simulations in `simulations`. Each gives the direction and preload (`fixed`; follower or axial, 0 = none), the specimens the studies used (`variants`: FSU, segment inside a multi-level specimen, L1-S1, L1-L5 or L1-L4) and the swept input: the pure moment (Nm), or the follower load (N) for the L1-S1 test at 8 Nm flexion / 6 Nm extension. Fix the caudal vertebra and load the cranial one. Report in degrees: rom_segmental = upper vs lower vertebra at each listed level, rom_total = cranial end vs caudal end, nz = neutral zone (rotation difference at 0 Nm on the third-cycle hysteresis, both directions summed; null if your model is elastic). One-direction simulations: neutral to peak; full-range ones (flexion+extension, L+R): sum of both directions at each moment. Run each simulation once, sweeping the input in `sweep` over all its listed values (start from the unloaded state; a denser curve is fine), and record every listed output. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one curve [[x, y], ...] per output (x = the sweep input; it is read by linear interpolation and listed x values outside your curve fail), or one number where there is no sweep or the output is marked scalar; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
